::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 20th [1900]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge XIII 1
:::

Dear [Mrs Belfield](people/person_133.qmd)
The precious mittens are safely come - it is a very curious genealogy for them - They are exactly like some little lace mittens of the 17th century figured in Mrs Earle’s[‘Child Life in Colonial days’](other_books/otherbook_756.qmd)

Madam Cromwell must been Elizabeth daughter of Richard who died at 83 in 1741 - Her mother, who was Dorothy Major of Hursley died in 1675 - so the mittens could not have been sent to her -[^1]

I will return them as soon as I have been able to shew them to a [cousin](people/person_28.qmd)of mine, devoted to King Charles and will in the meantime keep them safely

I knew Mrs Wynyard when she was living at Hursley. I was glad to hear she is so much better

Yours truly
C.M. Yonge

---

[^1]: Envelope addressed to ‘Mrs Belfield/Malmain/French hay /Bristol and postmarked Winchester 21 January 1900.
[^2]: The mittens had no doubt been sent to CMY in response to the account in *John Keble's Parishes* of the connection of the Cromwell and Major families with Hursley.
